paragraph:
What the Last Ferry Carried

On the morning Bell Island ceased to be an official place of (habitation), its oldest resident was trying to (whisk) an egg. The (yolk) broke, a gull gave a (shriek), and Ruth Calder announced that the government's timetable was (tosh). Her granddaughter Mina stood in the kitchen wearing a (mackintosh), holding a (rucksack), and attempting to (feign) patience. Outside, water had reached the village (sundial), and (condensation) blurred the windows. They watched water (gush) through a gap in the wall. The sea did not need to (countersign) the evacuation order. It had already begun to enforce it.

For three winters, engineers had measured an increasing (fluctuation) in the island's foundations. The report was (impersonal), its conclusion (bleak): another storm could (wreak) damage beyond repair. Residents had been offered mainland houses. Some regarded the offer as a (windfall); others called it an (abomination). Ruth called it organised (expulsion). Mina, whose job was to help everyone leave, knew that a fact could be correct and still fail to (quell) a person's (anguish). She put the pan down, resisting the urge to (straighten) everything within reach. “The last ferry leaves at four.”

Ruth became (waspish). Beneath a (tartan) (shawl), her shoulders seemed almost (frail), but her voice retained the power to (appal) a minister. She had a (knack) for repairing nets, developed over sixty years, and no talent for learning to (grovel). No grandchild would now (banish) her from her kitchen. Mina felt a (spasm) of (exasperation). She could organise an evacuation or win an argument with Ruth. Accomplishing both appeared unlikely.

The house contained seventy years of (handiwork). A (patchwork) quilt covered a (wickerwork) chair; a wooden (merman) grinned from the (lintel). On the shelf stood an (earthen) pot, a cracked (tureen), and a (cylindrical) tin of buttons. Ruth's husband had carved every (talon) of the seabird above the door, then forgotten its second eye. A (blemish) gave work character, she maintained. Mina thought it gave dust somewhere to (lurk).

A carved (yak) shared another shelf with a toy (sloth) and a glass (chameleon). Their owner had never travelled farther than the capital. These objects were a (constellation) of other people's journeys. A (smitten) sailor once gave Ruth a silver (flagon); she married somebody else and kept it. A wooden (weasel) came from a cousin whose stories could (hoodwink) nobody but himself. Mina had loved these things before she had to calculate their weight.

They agreed on three boxes. Ruth interpreted that as three per room. One held a (cauldron) from the village play, a (silken) scarf, and an (oaken) (chessman). Another contained a (phial) of perfume and a (vial) of something (whitish). A third carried a (candelabrum), a (quill), an (inkwell), and a (pincushion) shaped like a (toadstool). A dancer's costume exposing the (navel) joined them. The boxes were so (overladen) that lifting them looked like (heroism).

Under the table lay one (galosh), a model (toboggan), and a rusty (tenterhook) from the cloth workshop. Ruth wanted her husband's (chisel), too. He could (varnish) cupboards, (burnish) brass, and mend clocks, but paperwork defeated him. A (pinprick) of ink marked his final letter. Mina folded it carefully. The most important things were often the easiest to carry.

“Choose what matters,” Mina said. Ruth gave her a (baleful) look and added a (flannel). A garden (tendril) had entered beneath the (sill). Mina reached to (pluck) it free. Ruth caught her (forearm). “Leave that.” Her voice was (reproachful). Mina understood she was not defending a weed. Calling the move sensible would not (diminish) her loss. Every removal threatened to (heighten) her fear and (deepen) the belief that a whole life could become rubbish.

Mina went outside to (summon) help, leaving Ruth to (mull) her choices. The door gave a (creak); a frog answered with a (croak). A (lank) boy tried to (skulk) away from carrying boxes. His sister called him a (loon), then took the lighter end herself.

The square offered no (restful) alternative. Families tried to (cram) furniture into vans while children attempted to (gambol) between them. A (mongrel) escaped and began to (prowl) around the food stall. Somebody shouted about (vermin); another called it a (wastrel). The baker, an (unshaven) man in a (smock), still wearing his summer (suntan), told both to stop being a (pillock). His wife suggested “(berk)” was more accurate. Even in (turmoil), the village retained verbal precision.

A (sodden) notice described summer rainfall as “(subnormal)”. Someone had added a (scrawl): “It saved the rest for winter.” A man gave a (smirk); his wife answered with a (scowl). They had been told to (ration) drinking water in August. Now it was everywhere except where useful, producing considerable (resentful) humour.

At the harbour, Captain Noor worked with a (brisk) efficiency that made Mina (wistful). Wearing (khaki) trousers and a blue (turban), he could (beckon) a driver forward and (restrain) three passengers with one hand. The clerk tried to (deem) a piano ordinary baggage. A chain gave a (clank), a crate a (thunk), and a van a protesting (squeak). A (plank) covered a gap beside a truck's (flank). Every (berth) was assigned. There would be no second sailing.

A van arrived at (breakneck) speed and received Noor's wordless attention. Its driver began to (redden). This was no place to (careen) around children. A (jovial) volunteer tried to (liven) the atmosphere until he noticed the captain wasn't smiling. Noor was not on the (warpath). He wanted confusion to remain something less than injury.

A model (galleon) blocked the gangway. Its owner, a retired (barman), insisted it was culturally significant. Its sails could (unfurl), its cannon fired (confetti), and its paintwork would (astonish) collectors. Noor asked whether it floated. The man was taken (aback). “That's not the point.” Noor requested removal of the mast. The resulting (groan) sounded like a (sepulchral) bell. A fresh (dink) in the paint nearly caused an international incident. Nearby, a real boat tilted on its (keel), explaining why they were leaving.

After a (perusal) of the cargo list, Mina found the teacher beside a (sackful) of drawings. Miss Penn was a (disciplinarian) whose almost (paternal) concern sometimes exceeded her patience. She carried a (ream) of forms and a (pocketful) of confiscated marbles. A boy with one long (dreadlock) wanted to bring a rusty (javelin). His friend brought a (drumstick), although nobody owned a drum. Penn ordered the weapon put down (forthwith), then told the second boy to stop tapping.

He was Leo, her self-appointed (sidekick). His latest (contraption) combined a trolley and a kite. It could (propel) him downhill, though steering depended on luck. Penn repeated her (admonition) for the (umpteenth) time: no experiments near vehicles. Leo considered this an (insinuation) that his design was incomplete. It was, but that wasn't the main objection.

The children prepared a farewell (procession), wearing paper hats, a (garish) (wreath), and enough (tinsel) to (bedeck) a shop. One played a (warlock), another a (basilisk), and another a (ghoul) capable of an excellent (mewl). Their final (recital) was supposed to (hearten) parents, although the rehearsal's (commotion) hindered thought. Mina doubted a six-year-old (hangman) would improve morale. Penn removed a line promising to (disembowel) a dragon. The morning had enough threats.

The school contained a (hunchback) puppet, a wooden (gibbon), and a plaster (baboon) with a broken (beak) attached. The cupboard had never respected zoology. A sea-king costume resembled an (apparition); its (swollen) eyes and (misshapen) crown once left an inspector (dumbstruck). A (loincloth), an (elfin) cap, and a (shamrock) badge lay beside a (horseman)'s costume. The inventory labelled one missing head “(nonhuman)”. Mina wondered whether it would (enthral) a historian or (frighten) a warehouse manager.

Deputy Mayor Fenn arrived in a (mannish) coat with a (frill). Once called (fanatical) for demanding sea-wall repairs, she was now accused of enjoying the village's (downfall). She listened (noncommittal) while a fisherman delivered an (imprecation) involving “mainland (minion)”. Mina expected a (wrathful) reply. Instead, Fenn lifted his chair. Politics had taught her that (sarcasm) was lighter than furniture and less useful.

He insisted the mainland was a (pestilential) (pigpen). Fenn refused to (bludgeon) him with statistics. He was expressing (apprehension), not geography. His new house, she explained, had a ground-floor bedroom. That interrupted his (interrogation) long enough to move another box.

Ruth arrived dragging a (trowel), carrying a (pail). Mina allowed herself an (infinitesimal) hope that packing was finished. Then she saw the (shovel). Ruth intended to move her apple tree, planted by her husband on their wedding day. Its (blossom), she said, was better than any memorial (inscription). This was an unanticipated (complication). Mina stood (thunderstruck) while Ruth requested that she (kneel) and uncover the roots.

The tree stood on a (hillock), surrounded by (bluebell), (daffodil), and a determined (dandelion). Beyond it, (bracken) merged into (undergrowth), where a (quail) hid. The garden held (asphodel) and labelled (savin), kept away from children. A (hornbeam) had grown around wire, forming a (gnarl). Everything seemed attached to where it belonged.

A marker showed the next expected marine (incursion). Water would eventually (teem) with creatures needing no orchard. Mina disliked knowing that one landscape's destruction allowed another to (burgeon). The sea was neither a (crook) nor a rescuer. It favoured neither the (downtrodden) nor their (toil).

“The whole tree cannot go.” Ruth kept digging. A (torrential) shower turned the ground to (muck). Mina felt the wind (dishevel) her hair beneath her hood. Ruth's hands began to (stiffen); her (rheumatism) had worsened, though she would rather (perish) than admit it. Mina reached for the tool. Ruth gave it a (yank), striking Mina's arm and leaving a (weal). Both stopped. The possibility that a tool could (maim) had become suddenly (corporeal).

A year of (unspoken) worry had become a physical (chasm). Ruth looked (stricken). “I didn't mean—” Mina nodded. A drop fell from her sleeve with a (plunk); a gull gave a (squawk). The absurdity did not (lighten) anything. “I know.” Calling it an (overreaction) would only (deaden) the apology. Neither wanted the other hurt. That fact had to survive.

They sat on a wet bench. Ruth began to (bemoan) the move without enough strength to sound angry. Her husband had (lain) beneath the tree during his final summer. When breathing troubled him, she would (croon) an old song. The tree had witnessed tenderness they rarely expressed. She could not (fathom) leaving it to salt water. Mina had known the facts, not their meaning.

Ruth touched the handle as though it might restore his (footfall). “He never did things at the proper time.” Her voice held an unfamiliar (inflection): affection without a protective joke. The (recollection) quietened her. It wasn't theatrical (adoration), only the daily attachment whose absence she could never (accustom) herself to.

Mr Ives approached with a (flask) and a (bonbon). The accepted village (oddball), he wore a (cardigan) year-round and discussed roots until listeners became (glum). He examined the tree. “We don't need all of it.” Mina expected something (fanciful). He produced a grafting knife, precise as a (scalpel). Healthy cuttings could be grafted onto new rootstock. The original would remain, but its variety could (flourish) elsewhere.

Ruth listened with (mistrustful) concentration. Would it really be the same tree? Ives refused a comforting (delusion). It would be a new tree from the old, requiring care. Cuttings might (shrivel); some might fail. Gardening wasn't (divination). But it offered a better chance than uprooting a mature tree in rain. Mina watched (realisation) replace desperate (fixation): preserving something differed from refusing to (relinquish) anything.

They cut several shoots. Ives removed a (fleck) of bark and inspected a (pockmark). There was no serious (infestation). Healthy wood gave a pale (gleam), and rain made buds (glisten). Ruth gathered a (fistful) of paper around them and held one cutting to her (bosom). Her face showed neither (jubilation) nor defeat. “Your grandfather would call it cheating. Then he'd help.” A small (consolation) remained worth having.

At noon, the loading ramp reached a (standstill). Someone brought a stone (birdbath); another insisted a concrete (plinth) was an heirloom. A (vandal) sprayed farewell across the harbour wall. The mayor wanted it removed before reporters arrived. Noor suggested municipal (indignation) wait. A blocked ramp presented more immediate (peril).

Mina called the transport office from a (nook). Records of assistance needs were (uneven). One form seemed to (pertain) to a family already gone. She corrected it and added another name. People could fall (afoul) of systems without malice. Good intentions did not carry luggage.

The stone basin belonged to a butcher who considered refusal a (provocation). His breath suggested his (hipflask) was nearly empty. Weight limits became accusations of (favoritism), then threats of a (brawl). “People before stone,” Noor said. The butcher attempted a (headlock) on his laughing brother. It was (comical) and (pitiful). Mina and Fenn intervened.

A reporter approached, (agleam) with interest. One photograph could make this (ordeal) look like a riot. Nobody had gone (berserk), despite a broadcast calling villagers (hysterical). Fenn requested that he (abstain) from filming children. He protested that disorder was news. “Include the people preventing it.” There was (fraternisation) and help here, too. A lens could distort merely by choosing where to point.

A child began to (bawl), another to (snivel), and the dog to (howl). Its owner offered a (morsel) of (salami), immediately accepted. Human negotiations were harder. A woman gave a (disdainful) (snarl) at anyone near her wardrobe. A man wanted to (ransack) every van for his (haversack). A (scrum) formed by the scales. The harbour approached (bedlam), because every object seemed to contain the life its owner feared losing.

A youth jokingly tried to (frisk) another, provoking an accusation of (intimidation). Someone shouted “(hoodlum)”. The rise towards (pandemonium) reflected nerves, not criminality. Mina climbed a crate. She explained what could travel, what would follow, and what must remain. Promising universal safety was (guesswork); she would not do it. A (doleful) silence followed. Then Penn helped dismantle the wardrobe. Cooperation returned. The brothers began to (slink) away to carry their mother's bags. The (lull) was temporary. Mina had to (reckon) with fatigue as carefully as cargo.

The children performed. A girl with a (pigtail) delivered an (incantation) promising the island would never vanish. A boy dressed as a (yeoman) gave a (boastful) speech. The wizard attempted a (cartwheel), hit a chair, and landed on his (buttock). His (gleeful) audience applauded. A paper (jackal) lost its jaw; a cardboard (windmill) stopped. Leo's (pyrotechnical) finale produced a (swoosh), paper stars, and a (squeal). Nothing burned. Penn looked (awestruck). She hadn't wanted to (christen) the ferry with fire.

A man called the wizard a (buffoon). His wife said everyone needed foolishness. A leaving island required more than (trepidation). Children deserved something remembered as a (lark), not merely adults packing grief. Ruth laughed. Mina had forgotten her capacity for (mirth). A boy began to (twirl) a banner; a girl produced a (tuneful) (trill). Parents who had discussed (devastation) for months watched with tired (admiration). A performance couldn't rebuild a wall. It could make leaving more than administration.

Lunch included (haddock) sandwiches, boiled (whelk), (chilli), and a (muffin) for each child. One cook tried to (replenish) tea; another rescued a (saucepan) from an edge. Soap began to (froth) in a bowl. Somebody suggested seawater to (swill) plates; the cook said it would (befoul) them. Disaster still required distinguishing cleaning from worsening things.

Beside a roast (loin), gravy began to (congeal). A gull tried to (skim) it. The cook's (dustpan) proved an effective shield. A (swarm) of flies attracted one child's (revulsion) and another's interest. A teenager offered to (siphon) remaining water into bottles. Useful work could (dampen) panic better than orders to be calm.

Mina ate standing. A neck (crick) had become an (affliction); her eyes felt (feverish). The morning's (whirl) made her wish time would stop or (hasten). Asked by telephone whether progress was satisfactory, she replied, “Define satisfactory,” more (snappish) than intended. An (abysmal) answer about targets followed. She watched Ruth share food with a child. Some measures of progress deserved to remain unofficial.

Diesel fumes rose from the slipway, strong enough to (sicken). A line of (scum) marked the water. Mina pressed a (nostril) shut and breathed through her mouth. The harbour wasn't conspiring to (irk) her. Fatigue could turn any inconvenience into a personal attack, and she had seen where that led.

At two, an announcement caused (consternation). The mainland road was flooded; the ferry would use another dock, followed by buses. A wave of (desperation) crossed the queue. Small on a map, the change overwhelmed people who had exhausted their tolerance for uncertainty. A fisherman called the plan a (sham); his wife began to (wail). Another (repercussion) could matter more than the original disaster. Mina's (preoccupation) with loading nearly blinded her to that. She lowered her clipboard and listened.

Noor drew the route. The dock had shelter, toilets, and level access. Nobody would wait on a pavement. Specific, not (sensational), the explanation helped (dispel) rumours. He confirmed wheelchair space and wrote down a passenger's name. Trust began with a particular answer. A child's scarf made a (swish) against the board. Would monsters (loom) under the new dock? Probably crabs, Noor said. The answer disappointed the boy and relieved his mother.

The mayor requested Ruth for the cameras: the oldest resident, leaving with dignity. “She isn't a (talisman),” Mina said. His (roguish) smile and talk of morale were pure (smarm). She wanted to (hurl) the clipboard into the water. Instead, her refusal was (tactful) and absolute. She needn't vent her (spleen) at someone doing his job badly. He had the (gall) to call her unhelpful. Her jaw began to (tauten); she let it (slacken). Another fight wouldn't improve the crossing.

Ruth overheard and offered to speak, in her own words. The cameraman asked her to look positive. Her (jowl) tightened. “You can (zoom) out if my face bothers you.” She described the house, the tree, the ignored warnings. “This isn't magical (transfiguration). A new address doesn't turn grief into gratitude.” She would not (proclaim) victory or pretend denial could defeat the sea.

“We are going. That doesn't mean this was done well.” The mayor looked (crestfallen). Her words were (outspoken), angry, and accurate. They would probably (tarnish) a report. They might make the next village's experience less (woeful). The cameraman thanked her without requesting another take.

At three, people began to (embark). A (foal), travelling with a (roan) mare from the same (paddock), resisted until its handler loosened the (rein). A (fowl) escaped and gave a furious (cluck). Penn stopped two pursuing children. They didn't need poultry running (amok). Ives caught the bird beneath a coat and received a sharp (prick) for his trouble.

A dog gave a (growl); a cat answered with a (yowl). Their owner tried to calm both while shifting a bag. A (bloodstain) marked his collar: he had bitten his lip lifting furniture. The scene looked worse than it was, a useful reminder before another exaggerated report.

Ruth returned home once. The kitchen was (dank), its empty walls larger. A (footstool) stood by the cold (hearth); the (bellpull) hung motionless. She found a photograph and a brass key. It no longer opened anything she needed, but she pocketed it. Mina didn't ask her to justify something weighing almost nothing.

Ruth checked a lamp whose (wick) had been dry for weeks, then touched a pencilled height mark: Mina, aged nine. She closed the drawer. Neither spoke of (oblivion). A place could remain vivid when its rooms became unreachable.

Outside, a final (peal) came from the church. Wind began to (pummel) the hedge. A gull's (shrill) call crossed the garden; the apple branches turned silver. Mina felt a (premonition) that this scene would outlast forms and arguments in memory. Ruth's coat billowed. “Come on.” Her decision was (purposeful), and Mina followed.

On the slippery ramp, Ruth caught her shoe and began to (flail). Mina caught her. A (paroxysm) of fear passed. A medic checked for a (sprain): none, only a sore (toenail). Ruth called everyone dramatic. Noor looked (quizzical). “We prefer passengers attached to the ship.” A (dreadful) joke, but useful. Mina laughed with an (exhaustion) that resembled tears.

The engine gave a (clunk), a spoon a (clink). Water began to (slosh) against the hull. A boy tried to (dunk) a biscuit, producing a sticky (squish). A baby began to (drool) onto its father's coat. Another boy would (squirm) and (moan) about hunger. The father looked (sullen), then smiled when the baby caught his finger. Ordinary life had boarded already.

A deckhand began to (uncoil) rope. Another moved people clear: a tightening line could (whack) an ankle. This (precaution) needed no drama. Mina watched the last line fall, a (fateful) movement performed by someone who did it daily.

The ferry departed with a (whoosh). Its wake made a white (swirl); spray scattered in the (slipstream). Onshore, the flag began to (furl) around its pole. Mina expected a dramatic (swoon) of grief. Ruth merely asked whether the cuttings were upright. They were. Mina's eyes began to (brim). Ruth squeezed her hand without comment.

A boy asked whether ghosts would remain. Ruth said even empty villages needed caretakers. Mina left this thought unchallenged: comfort wasn't policy. The boy imagined a ghost with a broom, then a (reptilian) king living in the school. Imagination helped them bear what couldn't yet be explained.

The sea made passengers (recoil) from windows. A (sweetish) smell didn't help. Mina saw a woman's (complexion) turn (ashen) and offered a bag. Another passenger's (regurgitation) made everyone look away. Below, a (temperamental) pump complained. Asked what might (ail) it, the engineer declined to guess. He inspected and fixed it. The noise was mechanical, not prophetic.

A wave gave the hull a (smack). A child began to (gawk), while his brother announced they would sink. Penn stopped him with a look. They needed no invented (infernal) voyage. Rough water didn't prove that every possible disaster would (befall) them.

Ruth slept, her usually (watchful) face softening. Mina wondered what had taught her to equate surrender with death. War, poverty, a mother saving every (speck) of flour? History could (constrain) someone without announcing itself. Leaving required Ruth to argue with more than the government.

A fisherman began to (retell) a storm story involving lost trousers. A teenager gave a (catcall); Penn gave him a look. Someone sang. It was a rough (rendition), full of wrong notes, but the melody rose in an (unbroken) line. Ruth opened her eyes and supplied the forgotten words.

At the dock, volunteers offered maps and dry socks without banners. The lack of ceremony felt (merciful). Families could (disembark) without performing gratitude. Practical help required no spectacle of suffering.

A volunteer's (drawl) made Ruth lean forward. “Tea first.” She approved. A child instantly claimed an elaborate pink (confection). Small decisions could remain (uneventful). Today, that was luxury.

The temporary building's (multilevel) layout confused everyone. One resident called it a (hovel), another the carpet (phenomenal). Children found a broken (carousel) toy. An old man announced he could (loll) in his chair until Christmas. Mina tried to (unravel) a surname mix-up. By (nightfall), even an (eventful) day had to yield to supper. Someone complained about the carpet's (stink), another wanted to (preen) for a photograph, and a toddler tried to (sprawl) across three seats. Manageable problems.

Ruth inspected her room with a (dismal) face. “No sea.” Then: “No stairs either.” A (leaden) (gloom) lifted slightly. Not acceptance, but observation. They put the cuttings by the window. Ives promised pots. Nobody guaranteed growth. Nobody pretended otherwise.

An official message asked Mina to call the evacuation a successful transition. She deleted her first answer, containing an (allusion) to flying pigs. She couldn't (vanquish) official language with anger, but could refuse to repeat it. Her report described delays, the ramp, and useful assistance. It requested space for trees. This was not decoration, but part of continuing to live.

She named those who helped unasked. Reports could become weapons of (aspersion) or records of what worked. She chose the latter. The day contained failures and extraordinary effort; neither cancelled the other.

Ruth produced the brass key. “Your grandfather wanted to (bequeath) you the house. I suppose this remains.” Mina held it. She wouldn't call it enough. She would keep it. The metal seemed to (reawaken) the kitchen's smell without permission.

Over the following weeks, residents began to (bask) in the garden or (roam) nearby streets. Ruth learned the buses, argued with a shopkeeper, and acquired a difficult reputation before anyone could pity her. She wouldn't spend retirement in a (sulk), or permit anyone to call her anger (delusional). “I can dislike it and learn the bus route.”

After early (stagnation), Wednesday meetings considered a workshop and school garden. One man wanted to (repel) every official suggestion. Ruth said resistance wasn't a substitute for thought. They couldn't (pinion) their future to their worst day. She didn't pretend to have mastered that lesson herself.

The cuttings wintered in a protected bed. In spring, one bud opened. Ruth called Mina: no (bombshell) could sound more urgent. Her (exclamation) brought neighbours, one beginning to (exclaim) as though at a birth. A tiny leaf didn't repair the coast. It gave them tomorrow's task. Ruth announced that (henceforth), anyone calling it merely a stick would answer to her. Ives promised not to (deform) its growth with excessive wire or fuss.

Mina brought a camera. Ruth refused to pose and requested a watering can. The new leaves trembled. Behind them, residents argued about benches. Mina listened, smiled, and went to fetch the water.

贝尔岛正式不再被视为适宜(居住)之地的那天早晨，岛上最年长的居民正在(搅打)一枚鸡蛋。(蛋黄)破了，海鸥(尖叫)了一声，露丝·考尔德宣布政府的时间表简直是(胡说八道)。孙女米娜穿着(雨衣)，拿着(背包)，站在厨房里努力(假装)耐心。外面，海水已涨到村里的(日晷)，窗上满是模糊的(冷凝水)。她们看着水从墙缝里(涌出)。大海无须在撤离令上(会签)，它已经开始执行。

连续三个冬天，工程师都测到岛基越来越大的(波动)。报告(冷冰冰)，结论(黯淡)：再来一场风暴，就可能(造成)无法修复的损害。居民获配大陆住房，有人视为(意外之财)，有人称其为(令人憎恶的事)。露丝说，这是有组织的(驱逐)。负责协助撤离的米娜知道，事实即便正确，也未必能(平息)一个人的(痛苦)。她放下锅，忍住想把手边东西全部(摆正)的冲动。“最后一班渡轮四点开。”

露丝变得(尖刻)。披着(格子呢)(披肩)的肩膀显得(瘦弱)，声音却仍足以让部长(惊骇)。她修了六十年渔网，练就一身(本领)，唯独不会(卑躬屈膝)。孙女休想把她(赶出)厨房。米娜感到一阵(痉挛般的)(恼怒)。她可以组织撤离，也可以赢过祖母；同时完成两件事，似乎不大可能。

房子里积了七十年的(手工制品)。(拼布)被盖着(柳条编织的)椅子，木雕(男人鱼)在(门楣)上咧嘴笑。架子上有(陶制)罐、裂了的(汤盆)，以及装纽扣的(圆筒形)铁盒。露丝的丈夫把门上海鸟每一只(爪子)都刻得细致，却忘了第二只眼。她说，(瑕疵)使作品有个性。米娜觉得，它给灰尘提供了(藏身)之处。
